prompt: On a Linux router, packet forwarding for IPv4 has been enabled. After a reboot, the machine no longer forwards IP packets from other hosts. The command 'echo 1 > /proc/sys/net/ipv4/ip_forward' temporarily resolves this issue. Which one of the following options is the best way to ensure this setting is saved across system restarts?
choices: Run 'iptables -P FORWARD ACCEPT' and save the ruleset
Set net.ipv4.ip_forward=1 with sysctl -w at each login
explanation: Setting net.ipv4.ip_forward to 1 in /etc/sysctl.conf makes the kernel apply the parameter persistently at every boot.
